rationale: The Shootout matrix benchmark is a small, loop-intensive numeric kernel with no source-level functions or globals of significance, so the hot inner loops dominate both runtime and code-size concerns while the attack surface is the loop-body arithmetic and control flow. SUB is cheap, correct, and adds arithmetic diversity, so it gets the highest benefit weights with minimal cost penalties. SPLIT similarly carries near-zero runtime/size cost and fragments the loop control flow, aiding diversity cheaply. FLA and BCF are the strongest structural defenses but impose heavy dispatch/clone overhead exactly in the hot multiply-accumulate loops, so their high SecurityGain is offset by strong RuntimeCost/SizeCost penalties to keep them selective rather than blanket-applied. IBR and ICALL add indirection overhead on branches and calls that fire constantly in a numeric kernel, so they are kept at moderate benefit with elevated cost weights; IGV is nearly useless here (the program has essentially no global state worth hiding) and is effectively discouraged via low benefit and non-trivial cost weights, keeping overall overhead acceptable while preserving correctness.
